article_title: Tell us what you really think: undergraduate nursing students validation of the Questionnaire Virtual Patient - a qualitative think-aloud study.
citation: Mårtensson S, Eckerström J, Knez R, Sörman K, Larsson M. (2026). Tell us what you really think: undergraduate nursing students validation of the Questionnaire Virtual Patient - a qualitative think-aloud study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09738-y
title: Questionnaire Virtual Patient (QVP) instrument for evaluating virtual patient simulation in intimate partner violence education
description: The QVP is a questionnaire developed to evaluate an educational module on intimate partner violence focusing on virtual patient use. It comprises eleven background questions and eighteen additional questions structured into two themes: "(1) User friendliness virtual patient and (2) Virtual patient as an integrated part of educational module." Its design drew on the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, combining Likert-scale, slider-scale, and open-ended free-text formats.
requirements: Administration alongside the interactive educational module comprising a digital lecture, a virtual patient, and a dialog-based seminar
constraints: Refinements identified through cognitive validation prompted revised versions of most questions
target_learning_goals: Evaluating user-friendliness of virtual patient simulation and integration of learning didactics in intimate partner violence education
examples: The finalized version of the QVP, including background questions and revised questions from both themes, is provided in the Appendix.

title: QVP design grounded in Technology Acceptance Model and Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology
description: The QVP's design of standardized, comparable measures was "inspired by the Technology Acceptance Model [38] and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology [39] focusing on aspects such as user-friendliness, clarity of instructions and overall experiences using virtual simulation with virtual patient." These frameworks shaped the questionnaire's two themes and its mix of Likert-scale, slider-scale, and open-ended items. The article reports that students' generally positive perceptions align with this theoretical foundation.
requirements: Cross-disciplinary research team involvement in questionnaire development
constraints: The article notes inherent subjectivity in fixed numerical scales as a limitation of the quantitative scaling approach
target_learning_goals: Assessing acceptance and user experience of virtual patient simulation technology
